object_description: compact rectangular atrium building with roof terrace
design_condition: The compact rectangular building divides the site into two open areas, strengthens a pedestrian axis with paired squares, and reserves space for a later extension while keeping the site traffic-free.

positive.statement: The simple large building and specific public outdoor spaces make an interesting urban-planning contribution.
The protected outdoor workplace effectively showcases the institution's activities.
The building is clearly zoned, with prominent uses placed around the central area.
The flexible spatial layer supports different office, laboratory and practical-room configurations.
The compact shape creates usable land reserves and a favourable floor-area-to-envelope ratio.
The external appearance coherently corresponds to the rational floor plan and cubic structure.

negative.statement: After expansion, the remaining open areas would be overly open and mineral and would not meet all living needs.
The basement delivery arrangement requires a deep intervention into the ground and is complex.
The seminar-room floor has too little spatial quality because of its small foyer and long dark corridors.
The ramp and cascade staircase meet problematically in a confined space, and the staircase feels too small at the exits.
Requiring access through employees' open-plan offices is viewed as unfavorable.
The required floors and missing office and laboratory areas do not fit within the permitted building height.
The entrance level appears depressed in its proportions because of the truss-girder facade.
The atrium concept is not entirely convincing in its interior implementation.
